title: The repo-root manifest is the sole declaration of every secret the project needs
iWant: one file at the repo root that lists every secret the project depends on
soThat: I can see the dependency graph without grepping every deployable

acceptanceCriteria.description: A file `secrets.yaml` exists at the repo root and parses as YAML into an object with a `secrets` array; each entry carries a logical name, a per-environment path map, an owner, a rotationDays integer, and a required boolean.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a fresh clone of the repo
acceptanceCriteria.then: the loader returns a manifest object whose `secrets` array is non-empty and every entry has the fields `name`, `paths`, `owner`, `rotationDays`, `required`; no entry carries a `value` field

acceptanceCriteria.description: The Secrets Manager client refuses to serve a name that is not declared in the manifest.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a running process whose declared slice does not include the logical name `unknown-key`
acceptanceCriteria.then: the call throws a stable-coded `SECRETS_UNDECLARED_NAME` error naming `unknown-key` and no vendor call is made

acceptanceCriteria.description: A CI gate scans the source tree for code that reads a secret shape (an env-var name that appears in the manifest, or a call to a vendor SDK directly) and fails when a used name is not declared in the manifest or when a vendor SDK is imported outside the Secrets Manager module.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a change adds `process.env.THIRD_PARTY_TOKEN` to a source file and does not add `THIRD_PARTY_TOKEN` to the manifest
acceptanceCriteria.when: the CI gate runs on the change
acceptanceCriteria.then: the run fails with a stable-coded `SECRETS_MANIFEST_MISS` error naming the offending source path and the missing manifest name
